pr_title: feat: game control guide, the "?" in the top-right corner (#35)
copilot_review_summary: Copilot review: skipped by config/flag (no .vt/vt.config.yaml in this repo, so review.copilot_integration is not enabled). Visual E2E: covered by the local harness (validaciones/shell_generator/35: real Chromium, mouse / touch / keyboard at 9 sizes on Usuario and Objetivo, the owner's 125 % Windows case) and the owner's manual pass §1–§6. Verification pass: not run (no C/S findings); every finding was checked against the code before posting — the quality reviewer's worry that a row could span both halves of the screen doesn't hold (pairwise same-half grouping), so m3 is a comment. Security reviewer: no C/S findings (static strings by interpolation, hard-coded selectors and ids, no new dependency, bounded pointer map). Reviewers: 3 role-scoped `reviewer` instances (security, quality, documentation); m4 = D10 and m5 = D11 merged. Reviewed head: e6d1596.

findings.title: Spec comment claims leader lines never cross a control; row lines do
findings.description: `expectTidyLayout`'s comment says 'no line across a bubble or a control', but only line-vs-bubble is asserted, and a stacked row's leader starts on its control and runs past the stack: on phones the switch's line crosses the heat bar. That's intended (the owner saw it and passed manual §6), so the comment is what's wrong.

A.approach: Reword the comment: lines never cross a bubble; a stacked row's lines may pass over the controls stacked above.
A.rationale: Matches the behaviour the owner accepted and what the spec checks.

B.approach: Forbid row lines over other controls and defer such members to the lone path.
B.rationale: Changes the phone layout the owner approved; the stack would break on every phone.

C.approach: Assert line-vs-control only for non-row lines.
C.rationale: More test code for a rule nobody asked for.

findings.title: A clamped line position can leave a row bubble's arrow off its corner
findings.description: `lineX` is clamped to `anchor.left + 1`; for a control narrower than ~26 px or right of the previous line, the clamp lifts the line back within `LINE_SPACING` of its neighbour, so `leftBound` can pass `lineAt - ARROW_INSET`: the arrow sits off the bubble's corner (the component clamps the drawn arrow, so the leader line and arrow then disagree) and `maxWidth` can reach 0. No control that narrow exists today.

A.approach: When the clamp moves a line, place that member like a lone control (push it to `leftOver`); spec with two narrow stacked controls.
A.rationale: Falls back to tested paths; no new geometry.

B.rationale: Hides the symptom; the leader line still misses the arrow.

C.approach: Document that controls under ~26 px are unsupported.
C.rationale: Leaves a trap for the next screen.

findings.title: findRows' same-half rule isn't stated where placeRow relies on it
findings.description: `placeRow` takes `downward` from `row[0]` alone. The reviewer worried a chained row could span both halves; it can't — a stacked pair joins only when both are in the same half, so by transitivity the whole row is (level controls share a top) — but nothing says so next to `downward`.

A.approach: Comment at `downward`: every member of a row lies in the same half (findRows), so the first one decides.
A.rationale: Records the invariant the code relies on; no behaviour change.

B.rationale: Same result for every possible row; extra code.

findings.title: Comments still count ten bubbles on the game
findings.description: `callout.component.css` says 'The game's guide has ten bubbles' and the game spec's best-effort comment says 'ten bubbles don't fit'; since D8 the guide has nine.

A.approach: Say nine (or drop the count where it isn't the point).

B.rationale: Misleads the next reader about the bubble count.

findings.title: gameScreen fixture comment reads as a leftover
findings.description: After the D8 edit the comment reads 'Nuevo juego / Compartir (right). No bubble for the 3D view there. On one bottom row on wide screens; …' — two thoughts run together.

A.approach: Reflow into: what the screen has, where the rows go, and that there's no 3D-view item.

findings.title: The short-phone layout spec can't fail
findings.description: 'still places all nine bubbles on screen (best effort)' only checks the screen bounds, which the final clamp fallback guarantees for any input, so a regression that stacks every bubble on one point still passes. The name promises more than it checks.

A.approach: Rename to what it proves (a placement per item, clamped on screen) and add one real guard: every stackable row member is placed in its staircase (has a leader) at these sizes.
A.rationale: Honest name plus a check that fails if the stacked-rows path regresses on short phones.

B.approach: Ratchet: record each size's overlap count and fail if it grows.
B.rationale: Catches regressions but brittle to every font change.

findings.title: A spec hard-codes the 10 px gap
findings.description: 'keeps a bottom row's staircase near its row' asserts `rowTop - 10`; the 10 is `GAP` from geometry.ts.

findings.title: plan.md has no snapshot note and describes the pre-D7/D8 design
findings.description: The plan still says ten callouts, `#shell-region` over the visible shell, 3D-view aim; a reader takes it as the current design.

A.approach: Add a 'Plan snapshot note' under the Generated line (as #5 did): written 2026-09-29, before D7/D8; now nine callouts, no `#shell-region` on the game; see spec D7/D8.
A.rationale: Keeps the snapshot; points to the truth.

B.approach: Rewrite the plan to the current state.

findings.title: tasks record a 3D-view callout and #shell-region that D8 removed
findings.description: T003 (ten callouts incl. the 3D view), T005 (#shell-region, 3D-view aim) and T008 descriptions predate D8; nothing in the task record says so.

A.approach: Add `completion.notes` on T003/T005/T008: superseded by D8 (709aa40) — nine callouts, no #shell-region on the game; re-render tasks.md.
A.rationale: Keeps history, records the change where the task lives.

findings.title: Spec summary: 'ten controls or areas'
findings.description: Next to the 'nine bubbles' amendment, 'ten controls or areas' reads as a contradiction.

A.approach: 'nine controls and the 3D view, with no on-screen labels'.

B.approach: Keep it and add '(the 3D view has no bubble)'.

findings.title: Spec D2 is muddled after the amendment
findings.description: D2 says 'ten bubbles total … the issue body's "nine controls" count predates this; the guide has ten bubbles', then 'Amended: nine'.

A.approach: Selected option: 'one callout each (ten then; nine since D8)'; drop the 'predates' parenthetical.
A.rationale: One current count, history in brackets.

findings.title: Spec D3 still selects reuse for the 3D view
findings.description: 'reuse for the "?" and 3D view (selected)' — the game has no 3D-view bubble; it reuses the "?" and camera strings.

A.approach: 'reuse for the "?" and the camera (the 3D view's bubble was withdrawn, D8)'.

findings.title: Spec Testing Strategy: '3D-view bubble aims at the visible shell and re-aims on flip'
findings.description: Describes specs that no longer exist.

A.approach: Replace with 'no 3D-view bubble on either shell; a flip keeps the guide on'.

findings.title: Spec risk: 'Ten bubbles can't fit the shortest phones'

A.approach: 'The bubbles can't all fit the shortest phones (D7: best effort)'.
A.rationale: Current and points to the decision.

findings.title: Spec D7's '52-character limit' reads as current
findings.description: D7 says the switch line was shortened 'to fit the 52-character limit'; D8 raised the game's limit to 75.

A.approach: '…the then 52-character limit (75 since D8, for Compartir)'.

B.rationale: Loses why the switch line was shortened.

findings.title: Spec still presents the shell-region follow as part of the game's deliverable
findings.description: The shared helper is described as 'shell-region + tap-vs-drag'; the game uses only CanvasTap, followShell serves the initial screen.

A.approach: 'tap-vs-drag helper (CanvasTap, both screens) and the shell-region follow (followShell, the initial screen only)'.

findings.title: Spec header duplicated
findings.description: '<!-- vt.idd:spec --> ## Specification' appears twice (post-spec.sh added it on top of the draft's own).

A.approach: Remove the duplicate in the comment and the archive.

B.rationale: Harmless but sloppy; tag-based discovery still works.
